set.body:
Raised by independent review after Epic 0A closed.

The subtraction itself is CORRECT and matches the recommended inventory exactly:
- removed: correlation, cosine, covariance, fisher_z, rank_edges
- kept:    aggregate_first, reduce_partitions (live via measurement_form(reducer=)), inner_product (pinned default)
- .evaluate_edge_operation is gone entirely - zero references remain in R/ or tests/
- exports 72 -> 67; suite 0 fail, 0 error, 0 warn
No over-deletion found: the kept reducers still have 16 test references and measurement_form reducer coverage survives in test-effect-task-contract.R, test-coupling-views.R and test-evidence-task-ir.R.

Two gaps.

1. NO SUBTRACTION RECEIPT

Epic 0A acceptance states: "The reset records deleted exports, code, and tests as a subtraction receipt." No such artifact exists. No new markdown file was added, and grep for "subtraction" across *.md hits only the old searchlight-conversation-ledger.md. For the one epic whose entire output is deletion, the receipt is the only durable record of what was removed and why.

2. THE DELETED CODE IS UNRECOVERABLE

Verified with git log --all: neither R/operations.R nor tests/testthat/test-edge-operations.R was ever committed, and there are no stash entries. What is gone:

  tests/testthat/test-edge-operations.R   347 lines, deleted outright, never in git
  R/operations.R                          466 -> 179 lines, 287 removed, file never in git
  tests/testthat/test-bridge.R            242 -> 190 lines
  tests/testthat/test-pair-query.R        226 -> 185 lines

Roughly 725 lines removed from files that version control never knew about. There is no commit, no stash, and no receipt, so this cannot be reviewed, audited, or restored. If the deletion turns out to have been slightly wrong - one normalizer that should have been wired rather than dropped - there is nothing to compare against.

This is the concrete realization of bd-01KZXFZ4WRKASSWYMDSECG8FED, which carried a blocker note on this epic saying deletion is only safely reversible from a commit. It happened before any commit was made.

Suggested action

- Write the subtraction receipt now from whatever record still exists of the removed surface, even if partial; note explicitly where the original text is no longer available.
- Commit the tree. Every subsequent epic that deletes anything has the same exposure until that happens.
- Consider adding to Epic 9 acceptance that any epic whose output is deletion must produce its receipt before it closes.

The engineering decision was right. The evidence trail for it does not exist.
set.title: Epic 0A closed without its required subtraction receipt, and the deleted code was never in git
